items.title: Syrian president Ahmad Nami
items.notes: Ahmad Ibrahim Fakhri Nami (Damat Ahmet Nami). Married to Aysha, the daughter of Ottoman Sultan Abdul Hamid II. He was a prominent political figure who served as the second President of Syria and its fifth Prime Minister.

items.title: The Adyghe School in Syria
items.notes: Students at the Adyghe school in Quneitra, Syria, perform physical exercises outdoors in a stone-walled field. Established in 1934 under the leadership of Amin Samkough, this first Circassian school in the Golan Heights taught primary education, sports, and traditional heritage while preserving the native Adyghebze language.

items.title: Hadji-Khan Dzhandarov
items.notes: This historical photograph, cataloged as number 3504, was taken by the photographer Dmitry Ivanovich Ermakov between the 1870s and 1890s. The image captures Hadji-Khan Dzhandarov and a female companion, in Loovsky aul, an Abaza settlement located in the Kuban Oblast of the Russian Empire, which is known today as the village of Krasny Vostok in the Karachay-Cherkess Republic. Original prints and negatives from this ethnographic series are preserved today within the permanent collections of the ROSPHOTO State Museum and Exhibition Centre in Saint Petersburg. and some sources inform that this edition was a part of J. Guthrie Watson's album. J. Guthrie Watson (c. 1850–1913) was an English traveller. A member of the Conservative Club in London, Watson appears to have been a former military officer and was, in his words, “well acquainted with the Caucasus (particularly that portion known as Circassia).” In 1889 he embarked on a journey across the Russian Empire, which included Circassia in the North Caucasus. He published the photo-album “A Journey Across Russia” upon his return to England in 1889. It is not certain how many of the views in this album were photographed by Watson himself. In 1899 he exhibited a collection of photographs at the Anthropological Institute in London.

items.title: Issaq Zemzer Limpiz
items.notes: Al-Hajj Issaq Zemzer Limpiz (d. 1943) was a prominent Circassian community leader in Jordan. Renowned for his decorated service under the Ottoman Empire, he played a foundational role in Amman's civic development, famously donating his home to serve as the first headquarters for the Circassian Charity Association upon its founding in 1932.

items.title: Sharaf al-Din Rustam
items.notes: Sharaf al-Din Yehia Rustam (1897–1979) was a Jordanian officer of Circassian descent born in Wadi al-Seer. He achieved historical permanence by becoming the first officially registered soldier (Serial Number 1) in the foundational rolls of the Jordanian Armed Forces.

items.title: Batyrbek Bekmurazovich Shardanov
items.notes: Batyrbek Bekmurazovich (or Murzabekovich) Shardanov (1860–1937) was a prominent Circassian (Kabardian) nobleman, a pioneering civil engineer, an influential public intellectual, and a generous philanthropist. He holds a historic distinction as the first Kabardian railway engineer in the Russian Empire

items.title: Klishbi Aisovich Adzhigiriev
items.notes: Klishbi Aisovich Adzhigiriev (born 1876), a Kabardian man from the village of Nartan in the Chegemsky district, Kabardino-Balkaria. For the Soviet authorities, the social background of the Adzhigiriev family served as an indicator of "anti-Soviet sentiment." In December 1931, at the age of 55, Klishbi was arrested and accused of "preparing an armed uprising against Soviet power." In 1989, Klishbi Adzhigiriev was fully rehabilitated. Klishbi had six children; his wife was from the Ashabokov family. Two of his sons were executed by firing squad in 1937. Another son, Mukhametgeri, returned to the Kabardino-Balkarian ASSR after his period of exile.

items.title: The riders of the Abkhaz Hundred
items.names: Seated the third is Colonel Georgy Merchul
items.notes: The officers and riders of the Abkhaz Hundred, a volunteer cavalry unit formed in 1914 that served as the 4th squadron of the Circassian Cavalry Regiment within the Russian Empire's famous Caucasian Native Cavalry Division ("Wild Division"). Pictured during World War I in a formal studio setting with Colonel Georgy Merchul seated at the center.

items.title: Sasa Sagidovna Khurum
items.notes: This portrait captures Sasa Sagidovna Khurum from Pseituk in traditional Circassian festive attire with long split sleeves represent an ancient tradition, hanging loosely from the shoulder rather than serving as the modern, open-front pendants. This photograph remains a vital testament to a handcrafted family heirloom lost during wartime evacuation. The photo was taken at the Bolshoi Theatre in Moscow for the anniversary of the October Revolution.
